A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiteGS framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v2 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes readable method and experiment appendices A and B.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction-quality, training-time, rasterizer-performance and ablation results in Figure 1 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds cache measurements, parameter-budget analyses, per-scene and qualitative results, and an alternative-preprocessing experiment.

M1.justification: The core rasterizer, clustering pipeline and opacity-gradient variance/decay strategy remain unchanged. Limited corrections to the written algorithm include changing Morton quantization from 2^22−1 to 2^21−1 and Algorithm 1's quadratic coefficient from −0.5d to −0.5c. These establish specification corrections, without establishing an implementation redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate static-scene reconstruction on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples and Deep Blending. v3 presents its per-scene results as details of the retained benchmark comparisons. Additional parameter budgets and the subset/resampling experiment remain within this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds DashGaussian to Table 1, with a footnote attributing its metrics to the method's repository. Table 3 removes TC-GS from the backward-pass comparison by replacing its timings with dashes, while retaining its forward-pass results. The other existing comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 substantially expands parameter-budget evaluation through training/test PSNR curves across 13 scenes. B.4 adds a separate comparison excluding flowers and treehill and using PIL to downsample original images by four. These introduce additional evaluation designs; the main benchmark's stated GPU, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and Garden budget plot, v3 tests the memory-locality explanation with L2-cache trajectories in Figure 3, examines budget-dependent fitting and generalization across scenes in Figure 6, adds visual case studies in Figure 7, and checks preprocessing sensitivity in Table 6. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental uncertainty estimates. v3's additional per-scene values and training/test curves remain point estimates; the opacity-gradient variance is a method component, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial per-scene, budget-sweep, cache, qualitative, DashGaussian and alternative-preprocessing results, while retaining most original aggregate scores. It changes Table 4's Mip-NeRF 360 w/o Var SSIM from 0.789 to 0.813 and Table 1's caption SSIM from 0.780 to 0.870. TC-GS backward timings of 1.53, 4.09 and 9.28 ms are removed. Table 6 represents additional results under different preprocessing, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit scanline forward/backward derivations and instruction-count reasoning for the existing optimization. v3 also corrects the transmittance recurrence to use the preceding primitive's opacity and distinguishes the tile count from the camera count in Equation 3. These are localized mathematical additions and corrections; the central densification definition is retained.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution statement changes the roughly 10.8x comparison from the 'SOTA acceleration solution' to the 'quality SOTA solution,' aligning its scope with the 3DGS-MCMC comparison. The three central technical contributions, 13.4x acceleration claim and high-quality reconstruction claims otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains discrepancies with published MCMC/SSS scores through preprocessing differences. Appendix A.3 adds a concrete explanation of how 32-byte memory sectors limit sparse-update savings. It also removes the speculative RTX 5090 seconds-level training statement. The existing limitations concerning center-only Morton sorting, dynamic scenes and mobile deployment remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact instructions for the alternative preprocessing, per-scene primitive budgets and timings in Table 5, and details such as compile-time scanline constants and memory-sector granularity. It discloses the external source of DashGaussian's metrics. The repository link, principal hardware disclosure and main training schedule are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DashGaussian citation and discusses its speed/quality relationship to TamingGS. It explicitly positions TC-GS as an inference method in Table 3. The broader acceleration and densification literature discussion and LiteGS's central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence closely follow v2, with localized grammar, terminology and heading edits. v3 introduces numbered subsections and appendix cross-references, relocates Algorithm 1 and supporting material, and organizes additional explanations and experiments into appendices. The existing prose is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document from two-column to single-column layout and restructures Tables 3 and 4. The earlier cluster pipeline Figure 2 is redrawn and relocated as Figure 5. New gradient/culling diagrams, cache and parameter-sweep plots, qualitative image comparisons, and Tables 5–6 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the explicit derivations, cache diagnostic and matched-preprocessing experiment make LiteGS easier to understand and assess. However, the new per-scene reporting introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Table 5 gives 3DGS-MCMC Deep Blending LPIPS values of 0.234 and 0.236, while Table 1 reports 0.320 without explaining the difference. The added support and corrections provide a net benefit, but these reporting problems limit the overall improvement.
